2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 25.6476% (JSC: 26.678 mA/cm², VOC: 1.1799 V, FF: 81.4827%). 1.65 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with the composition of Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 was prepared. The perovskite precursor solution was dripped onto the substrate, and a two-step spin-coating procedure was applied. The first step was carried out at 1000 rpm, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. Then, 150 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the second spin-coating step at the last 15 s of the spin-coating. Thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min improved crystal ordering and reduced defect density.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells are achieved through precisely engineered crystallization kinetics and comprehensive defect management, beginning with the Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3 triple-cation composition which optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor and lattice entropy for enhanced phase stability and a favorable bandgap. The crystallization process, governed by a 1.65 M precursor concentration and a two-step spin-coating procedure culminating in chlorobenzene antisolvent dripping at a critical 15-second mark, promotes rapid and homogeneous nucleation, a mechanism further refined by the subsequent 110°C thermal annealing which drives Ostwald ripening for improved crystal ordering and reduced bulk defect density. This meticulous control over film formation is directly evidenced by characterization: uniform photoluminescence emission maps indicate spatially homogeneous carrier recombination and minimal non-radiative trap clusters, while X-ray diffraction patterns showing dominant perovskite phase peaks with suppressed PbI₂ signatures at ~12.6° and narrow full-width-at-half-maximum values corroborate high crystallographic purity, large grain growth, and the effective mitigation of residual lead iodide and strain-related defects. The resultant high-quality perovskite absorber, characterized by these superior morphological and structural properties, enables efficient charge transport and extraction, ultimately yielding a champion power conversion efficiency of 25.6476% with a short-circuit current density of 26.678 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage of 1.1799 V, and a fill factor of 81.4827%.
